title: Predictive Warmup Evaluation: GPU Pre-provisioning Tests (May 2026)
summary: Series of compact spreadsheet-driven experiments to compare predictive pre-provisioning (scheduled warmup) against reactive min/max autoscale across regions and workload shapes. Objective: measure p95 latency, cold start rate, and end-to-end cost delta for realistic morning ramp and bursty traffic patterns.

conclusions: Predictive pre-provisioning (scheduled warmup) consistently reduced p95 latency and cold-start rates versus reactive min/max across all tested regions.

Cost delta was negative (cost savings) in larger pools (standard-8) when warmup timed to the ramp window due to fewer failed retries/long tail latency penalties upstream, but small pools saw smaller or negligible savings.
Warmup duration tuning is critical: too-short warmup only reduces cold starts partially; too-long warmup increases idle cost without proportional latency gains.
Quantized model pools benefit more from warmup (faster instance readiness), making predictive warmup a lower-cost win for quantized-serving lanes.
Predictive strategy reduced burst cold-start storm scenarios (APAC tests) and improved downstream tail behavior for client-facing routes.
Operational complexity: scheduling windows + model-version awareness required to avoid unnecessary provisioning when rollouts are in progress.
action_items: Prototype an autoscaler feature flag 'predictive-warmup' that accepts (region, pool, window-start, window-end, warmup_seconds). Owner: Diego Ramos. ETA: 3 weeks.
Add telemetry hooks to measure instance readiness time and model-load duration per pool (needed to auto-suggest warmup_seconds). Owner: Maya Singh. ETA: 2 weeks.
Run extended 30-day experiment on US & EU standard pools with model-version pinning to validate cost signals. Owner: Noah Kaplan. ETA: Q3 2026.
Draft runbook for scheduling warmup windows during business-critical ramps (marketing events, enterprise windows). Owner: eng-sre. ETA: 1 week.
Surface predictive-warmup as an opt-in policy in Redwood Console with recommended defaults per pool type. Owner: product-console. ETA: roadmap discussion.
Instrument A/B on a small subset of customers to quantify user-visible latency improvements and incidents avoided. Owner: solutions-eng. ETA: 6 weeks.
notes_and_open_questions: How does predictive warmup interact with canary/rollout policies? We observed cases where warmup provisioned instances with old model version during rollout—need model-aware gating.
Should warmup be model-size aware (derive warmup_seconds from measured model load time)? Preliminary telemetry suggests yes.
What are acceptable cost thresholds for dedicated customers vs hosted? Potentially expose warmup-cost tradeoff in Console.
Edge case: sudden off-hour burst (true surprise) where predictive warmup cannot help—combine with reactive rapid-burst path.
